LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 10.3.1 WORD CLASSES: DEMONSTRATIVES AND QUANTIFIERS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.3: Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers, part of Strand 10 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use demonstratives and quantifiers? 2. When do we use demonstratives and quantifiers?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify quantifiers (few and many) and demonstratives (this, these and that and those),

2. point out various items that are at different distances,

3. determine the correct demonstratives to use in different circumstances,

4. generate the plural forms of the demonstrative pronouns, with peers,

5. demonstrate practically the differences in meaning in quantifiers such as little and a little amount of water,

6. generate sentences using various demonstratives and quantifiers,

7. construct sentences using demonstratives and quantifiers from a substitution table. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify quantifiers (few and many) and demonstratives (this, these and that and those),
2. point out various items that are at different distances,
3. determine the correct demonstratives to use in different circumstances,
4. generate the plural forms of the demonstrative pronouns, with peers,
5. demonstrate practically the differences in meaning in quantifiers such as little and a little amount of water,
6. generate sentences using various demonstratives and quantifiers,
7. construct sentences using demonstratives and quantifiers from a substitution table. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Demonstratives and Quantifiers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: It is promoted as the learner works in a team to generate the plural forms of the

demonstrative pronouns with peers.

• Self-efficacy: It is developed as the learner practices the correct use of demonstratives and quantifiers.

Values:
Love: It is exhibited through care and compassion as the learner works with peers to generate the plural forms of the

demonstrative pronouns.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Critical thinking: It is enhanced as the learner uses logical thinking selects the correct demonstratives and quantifiers to use in

different contexts.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Determiners and quantifiers are concepts that are related to learning of word classes in Kiswahili.
